name: AM26LS31CDR
title: AM26LS31, AM26LS31M: quadruple differential line driver, TIA/EIA-422-B, 5 V, three-state outputs
summary: Four RS-422 line drivers in one package, each turning a TTL input into a complementary Y/Z output pair able to drive twisted-pair lines. A shared pair of enables (G active high, /G active low) puts all outputs into high impedance, and they stay high impedance with the power off. The AM26LS31C runs from 4.75 V to 5.25 V, and the AM26LS31C and AM26LS31I are rated for −40 °C to 85 °C; the AM26LS31M, offered to MIL-PRF-38535, runs from 4.5 V to 5.5 V at −55 °C to 125 °C. Packages are SOIC, SSOP, PDIP and SO for the commercial parts and CDIP, CFP and LCCC for the military ones.

circuits.title: Figure 8-1. Encoder application
circuits.description: A servo drive sends an encoder's signals to a motion controller over four twisted pairs. The encoder interpolation electronics' A, B and Z outputs and a status line enter drivers 1 to 4 of the AM26LS31. Each driver's Y output runs on one wire of its pair to the non-inverting input of a channel of an AM26LS32 receiver, and its Z output on the other wire to the inverting input; a resistor across each pair at the receiver terminates it. The receiver outputs are the controller's encoder phase A, phase B, index and status.

circuits.title: Figure 6-1. Switching test load
circuits.description: The load an output sees while its switching times are measured. CL to ground sits on the output, which is also the test point. Switch S1 connects 180 Ω to VCC and switch S2 connects 75 Ω to ground. Both switches are open for propagation delay and skew; enable and disable times use one or both closed.

parts.note: 30 pF or 10 pF per the switching tables, probe and fixture included

operation.text: Four differential line drivers for one-way data over balanced pairs (twisted or parallel wire), meeting TIA/EIA-422-B and ITU V.11 from one 5 V supply. Each driver turns a TTL-level input A into a complementary pair: Y follows A and Z is its inverse.
G (active high) and /G (active low) are shared by all four drivers. The outputs drive when G is high or /G is low; with G low and /G high all eight outputs are high impedance.
The three-state outputs are high impedance when disabled and also when the supply is off.

Each driver sources or sinks at least 30 mA and limits its current in both directions against line faults. Short-circuit current is −30 mA to −150 mA; short only one output at a time and for no longer than one second.

In the PDIP, SO, SOIC and SSOP packages the power-on-reset threshold on a rising supply is 2.27 V to 3.04 V (2.48 V typ) and the brown-out-reset threshold on a falling supply is 2.03 V to 2.26 V (2.13 V typ), with 350 mV typical hysteresis between them.

The equivalent circuit of each driver uses low-power Schottky circuitry, with nominal 9 Ω resistors in the Y and Z output stages, a nominal 22 kΩ resistor at input A, and two nominal 22 kΩ resistors in the enable circuit common to all four drivers.
The AM26LS32 is the matching receiver; any receiver meeting RS-422 works with the driver.

RS-422 has a single driver on a line, so a termination, if fitted, sits only at the receiving end, next to the last receiver; RS-485 usually terminates both ends. The choices are no termination, parallel, AC and multipoint termination, weighed on performance and cost. Bench waveforms were taken with an AM26LS31CN-E and an AM26LS32C over 100 ft of 100 Ω 24-AWG twisted pair at room temperature and 5 V.

The encoder example runs from 5 V at 10 Mbps or less, with a connector that keeps the pair polarity right. Mount the driver near the bus connector so the stub is short. Optional fail-safe bias can hold 200 mV across the pair while the driver is high impedance.
A 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic capacitor goes from VCC (pin 16) to ground as close to the device as possible; one capacitor serves a single supply.

Use a ground plane, keeping digital and analog ground currents apart. Keep input traces short and away from supply and output traces, crossing them at right angles where they must cross, and keep logic signal traces short. Place external parts close to the device.
